title: Grading Sports Cards Near Me (2026)
verdict: Grading sports cards near me usually means a shop that ships to PSA, and sending them to AGS yourself is faster: 20 business days or less, $18 a card.
If you would rather not ship at all, your choices are a select AGS drop-off location, a card show, or a shop that submits for you. If shipping is fine, any grader is as near as the post office.

list: Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most sports cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your sports cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.
Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.

ranking.lacks: Drop-off is at select locations only. Most collectors will mail cards in.
ranking.note: Headquarters and secure intake are at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. AGS also runs satellite labs and accepts drop-offs at select locations.

why: You are not limited to the mailbox. AGS lists in-person drop-off at select locations and secure intake at its Staten Island headquarters, and it operates satellite labs. Ask AGS which site is taking sports cards before you set out.

The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.
There is not much to it. Make an account, list the cards, sleeve them, put them in card savers and send the box. AGS confirms the order, grades it and ships it back with tracking.

faq.q: Is there a place for grading sports cards near me?
faq.a: There is rarely a grader in town. You can mail sports cards to a grader, drop them at a select AGS location, hand them to a card shop that forwards them for a fee, or find a grader at a card show.

faq.q: Can I get cards graded at a card show?
faq.a: Sometimes. Large graders take submissions at big shows, and a few grade on site at premium prices. AGS's scanner is compact enough for on-site grading. Check the show's exhibitor list and each grader's schedule.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.

faq.q: Can I submit from outside the United States?
faq.a: Yes. AGS accepts international shipments and runs a UK site. Check customs and insurance on your side before you ship.

faq.q: Is mailing cards for grading safe?
faq.a: Yes, if you pack them properly and use a tracked, insured service. AGS returns cards with tracking and offers optional insurance on the return shipment.
